Every point carries the change and the percentage change on the one before, and the result carries the highest, the lowest, the average and the change across the whole period - so a chart or a trend alert needs no arithmetic of its own. Where the figures are already percentages the change is given in points instead, because the percentage change between two percentages is not a number anybody wants. The filters have to pin the dataset down to a single series; if they do not, the step says which box is still open. Covers the last 24 periods unless you set dates.

This is the way in to everything the headline statistics do not cover: trade by partner country, financial soundness indicators, reserves, government finance, the Financial Access Survey. Half the catalogue is dated archive copies frozen as a published report left them; those are left out unless you ask for them, and the result says how many.

description: Read the IMF's official economic statistics from a workflow. Get growth, inflation, unemployment, GDP, government debt and deficit, the current account, population or the exchange rate for any of roughly 200 economies, follow one through time, compare countries side by side, or pull a whole country profile in one step. World commodity prices - crude oil, gold, copper, wheat, coffee - come from the IMF's own price system. Everything else the IMF publishes, from trade by partner country to financial soundness indicators, is reachable by searching the catalogue and filtering a dataset by name. The World Economic Outlook publishes forecasts beside measurements, so every figure says which it is. Every action reads: nothing here changes anything. No account or API key required.
